issues.title: Your website uses secure HTTPS
issues.description: SSL encryption is active across your domain, protecting visitor privacy and fulfilling Google's core baseline.
issues.whyItMatters: Satisfies Google's core ranking security requirement and builds immediate trust with visitors.
issues.recommendedAction: Maintain auto-renewal of your SSL certificate.

issues.title: Missing robots.txt file
issues.description: No robots.txt file was found at the root of your domain (e.g. /robots.txt returned 404).
issues.whyItMatters: While not mandatory, robots.txt tells Google which pages to prioritize and points crawlers to your XML sitemap.
issues.recommendedAction: Create a simple robots.txt file at the root of your server referencing your sitemap.

issues.title: XML Sitemap could not be found at /sitemap.xml
issues.description: Search crawlers could not locate an XML sitemap at the standard /sitemap.xml location.
issues.whyItMatters: Without a sitemap, Google might miss secondary service pages or take weeks to discover new blog posts.
issues.recommendedAction: Generate an XML sitemap using your CMS (WordPress Yoast/RankMath, Shopify, or a generator) and submit it to Google Search Console.

issues.title: 1 broken link(s) detected
issues.description: During crawling, 1 internal URL(s) returned HTTP errors (404/500).
issues.whyItMatters: Broken links frustrate customers and signal to Google that the website is outdated or poorly maintained.
issues.recommendedAction: Update or remove broken internal links or set up 301 redirects to the correct active destination.

issues.title: Homepage title does not clearly target your service or location
issues.description: Your current homepage title is "Error: fetch failed". It lacks your primary local keyword ("Nowhere") or primary service offering.
issues.whyItMatters: When local customers search on Google (e.g. "${primaryService} in ${cleanLoc}"), Google matches their search intent against your page title.
issues.recommendedAction: Rewrite your homepage title to combine your brand name, core specialty, and primary city.

issues.title: Missing meta description on homepage
issues.description: Your homepage does not have a <meta name="description"> tag.
issues.whyItMatters: Google will pull random fragments of text from your page, resulting in an unappealing search snippet that loses clicks to competitors.
issues.recommendedAction: Add a 130-160 character meta description highlighting your services, location, and a clear call to action.

suggestedFix.recommended: Looking for top-rated restaurant in Nowhere? Total Nonsense delivers reliable, professional service. Contact us today!

issues.title: Homepage is missing an H1 main heading
issues.description: No <h1> heading was detected on your homepage.
issues.whyItMatters: The H1 heading is the primary structural landmark of your page. Google uses it to verify the core subject matter.
issues.recommendedAction: Add a prominent <h1> heading near the top of your page containing your business name and main service.

issues.title: Missing LocalBusiness structured data (Schema.org)
issues.description: Your website does not include machine-readable Schema markup for local businesses.
issues.whyItMatters: Structured data explicitly informs Google of your official business name, coordinates, category, and contact numbers, significantly improving your presence in the Google Local 3-Pack and Knowledge Panel.
issues.recommendedAction: Paste a valid LocalBusiness JSON-LD script into the <head> of your website.

issues.title: Weak local signals for "Nowhere" across your website
issues.description: Your target city or region ("Nowhere") is only mentioned on 0 page(s).
issues.whyItMatters: Google relies on local relevance signals to determine geographic ranking boundaries. Weak location signals make it hard to rank outside your immediate street.
issues.recommendedAction: Incorporate natural mentions of Nowhere, your neighborhood, and surrounding areas in your page footers, about page, and service descriptions.

issues.title: No dedicated contact page found
issues.description: We could not find a page with "contact" in its URL or internal links pointing to a contact page.
issues.whyItMatters: Google uses contact consistency as a local trust signal, and customers look for an easy way to reach you.
issues.recommendedAction: Create a contact page with your business name, address, phone number, and a clickable tel: link.
